problem: The inequality is broken: it reads "for every w in W with w ≠ p, ‖b−p‖  ‖b−p‖²", with the comparison sign missing and the right-hand side wrongly written as ‖b−p‖² instead of ‖b−w‖. As printed the sentence states no property and a student cannot tell what is being claimed.
fix: For every w in W with w ≠ p, ‖b − p‖ < ‖b − w‖ (equivalently ‖b − p‖² < ‖b − w‖²). The projection p is the unique closest point of W to b.

problem: The question asks for the three matrix properties of an orthogonal projection matrix, but the given answer lists P = QQᵀ (a formula for one particular construction of P, not a property) together with only two properties. It does not match the three properties stated in Section 1 (P² = P, Pᵀ = P, and P projects onto col(Q)).
fix: Answer: P² = P (idempotent), Pᵀ = P (symmetric), and P maps every vector onto col(Q), the subspace it projects on. When Q has orthonormal columns, P is written explicitly as P = QQᵀ.

problem: The last term of the sum is printed as "em²" instead of e with subscript m, so the expression looks like the product e times m squared.
fix: ‖e‖² = e₁² + e₂² + … + e<sub>m</sub>², where m is the number of rows of A.

problem: Node p is labelled "p = QQᵀb" while its note says "closest point in col(A)". QQᵀ projects onto col(Q), which equals col(A) only when Q is an orthonormal basis of col(A); the figure does not say this, so the two labels read as inconsistent.
fix: Label the node "p = QQᵀb = Ax̂" with the note "closest point in col(A), where Q is an orthonormal basis of col(A)".

problem: "A projection drops a vector straight down onto a subspace" suggests a vertical drop, which is only the picture for a horizontal subspace. In general the drop is perpendicular to the subspace, in any direction.
fix: "A projection drops a vector perpendicularly onto a subspace and keeps the closest point."
